newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says no plans to sell Port Kembla unit.
newsitem.headline: BHP says no plans to sell Port Kembla unit.

text.p: Australia's largest company and biggest steelmaker, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), said on Thursday that it did not plan to sell the packaging products operation at its Port Kembla steelworks south of Sydney.
"We are definitely not selling our packaging products division," a BHP Steel spokeswoman said.
Australian Broadcasting Corp radio earlier quoted a politician from the New South Wales (NSW) state legislature who said BHP planned to sell the operation to British Steel Plc.
BHP has said it would expand the operation, which makes tin-coated steel for use in manufacture of food cans and paint tins.
By the year 2000, BHP planned to boost output from the Port Kembla tin mill by 40 percent to 500,000 tonnes a year, the company spokeswoman said.

Newspaper reports said NSW politician Tony Stewart told state parliament that he had seen documents which said BHP managing director John Prescott had recently met British Steel executives in Singapore.
Stewart said he believed a deal was now in the last stage of negotiation.

The Port Kembla steelworks have been singled out for expansion by BHP under its recently released national steel plan which will end raw steelmaking at Newcastle, north of Sydney, in 1999 at a cost of 2,500 jobs.
